story_type: controlled explosion breaches a century-old river dam
hook: This dam held back a river since 1907. Then they blew it open.
narration: This dam held back a river for more than a century. Then the Army blew a hole in it.
Locks and Dam three sits on the Monongahela River near Elizabeth, Pennsylvania, and it had been running since nineteen oh seven.
It was prone to flooding, and it shut down in high water, delaying the barges.
For a controlled blast, crews pack explosives into holes drilled through the concrete, then fire them in a rapid sequence.
On July tenth, two thousand twenty four, the Army Corps of Engineers set off the first charge, with the river closed fifteen hundred feet on each side.
[short pause] And it was only the first. Thirteen more blasts would take down the rest in fifty foot sections.
outcome: The first charge breached the old dam, the start of one open river pool thirty miles long.
title: Blowing up a dam from 1907
description:
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Pittsburgh District sets off a controlled explosion to breach the fixed-crest dam at Monongahela River Locks and Dam 3 near Elizabeth, Pennsylvania, on July 10, 2024, the first of a series of blasts to remove it.
